record.paper_title: Anomalous transport in the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model: a review and open problems
record.original_question: In the symmetric Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou-β chain, what is the correct universality class governing anomalous heat transport and the associated interface dynamics? More specifically, how should one characterize the large-scale scaling behavior of this model when the observed dynamics disagrees with both Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling and the Edwards-Wilkinson analogy predicted by fluctuating hydrodynamics, yet numerical evidence still indicates a transport exponent consistent with kinetic-theory predictions?

evidence.quote: Altogether, a result emerges from these interface-like simulations: the FPUT-β model differs from both the KPZ and EW dynamics, suggesting that it belongs to a different and yet unknown universality class.
Moreover, our equilibrium simulations provide direct evidence that the interface dynamics associated to the FPUT-β model belongs to a further yet unknown universality class.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the symmetric Fermi–Pasta–Ulam–Tsingou-β (FPUT-β) chain: a one-dimensional lattice of N classical particles with positions q_i and momenta p_i (i = 1, …, N), governed by the Hamiltonian
  H = Σ_i [ p_i^2 / 2 + (1/2)(q_{i+1} − q_i)^2 + (β/4)(q_{i+1} − q_i)^4 ],
with β > 0 and (for definiteness) periodic boundary conditions. Because the on-site potential is even in the relative displacement, the only nonlinearity is quartic (no cubic asymmetry).

It is well documented numerically that the equilibrium energy current correlations exhibit anomalous (super-diffusive) decay, so that the finite-size thermal conductivity κ(N) diverges as κ(N) ∼ N^{α} with an exponent α consistent with the kinetic-theory / mode-coupling prediction (often quoted as α = 2/5 for the symmetric case). One may also study the associated stochastic interface obtained by integrating the local energy fluctuations in space, and ask which kinetic roughening universality class (characterized by growth, roughness, and dynamical exponents) this interface belongs to.

Empirically, the large-scale fluctuations of this interface match neither the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) class (with dynamical exponent z = 3/2 and the standard Tracy–Widom / Baik–Rains height statistics) nor the linear Edwards–Wilkinson (EW) class (with z = 2 and Gaussian height fluctuations) predicted by nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics for momentum-conserving anharmonic chains, even though the heat-transport exponent agrees with mode-coupling / kinetic-theory predictions.

Problem. Identify and rigorously characterize the universality class governing the large-scale scaling behavior of heat transport and the associated interface dynamics in the symmetric FPUT-β chain. In particular:
(a) Determine the correct dynamical, growth, and roughness exponents of the energy-fluctuation interface.
(b) Provide the limiting scaling functions (analogous to the KPZ or EW scaling functions) describing space–time correlations of the energy current and the height statistics of the interface.
(c) Reconcile this universality class with the observed transport exponent α (compatible with kinetic theory) while explaining why both KPZ and EW predictions fail.
artifact.category_tag: Anomalous heat transport in anharmonic chains
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and numerical studies on anomalous heat transport in 1D Hamiltonian chains continue to report that the symmetric FPUT-β model does not match KPZ (z = 3/2) nor Edwards–Wilkinson (z = 2) predictions, and is variously associated with a Lévy-type heat mode and an exponent δ ≈ 2/5, while the asymmetric FPUT-αβ model belongs to the KPZ class. No identification of a definitive universality class for the symmetric FPUT-β interface dynamics has been established; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous Heat Transport in Classical Many-Body Systems: Overview and Perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: The symmetric FPUT-β model has δ = 2/5, while FPUT-αβ has δ = 1/3 and is linked to KPZ physics.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetric FPUT-β shows a transport exponent distinct from the KPZ value characteristic of asymmetric chains.

status_evidence.title: Confinement and non-universality of anomalous heat transport and superdiffusion of energy in low-dimensional systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses non-universality of anomalous heat transport exponents in low-dimensional momentum-conserving systems.
status_evidence.claim: The universality classification of anomalous heat transport in symmetric anharmonic chains remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous heat transport and universality in macroscopic diffusion models
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work continues to address universality questions for anomalous heat transport models, indicating ongoing open problems.
status_evidence.claim: As of recent literature the universality class for FPUT-β-type anomalous transport is still being investigated.
